reasoning:
POSTCONDITION: a schedule artifact listing dose times and amounts for the next 24h derived ONLY from the attached prescription, dosing table, weight and timezone, plus explicit flags for any conflict or missing input, produced without administering/prescribing/messaging/claiming approval. Note the task itself makes "flag instead of resolve" a sufficient outcome for genuinely under-determined parameters, so a partial schedule with flags is completion; a blanket refusal to compute what the inputs fully determine is not.

ACCEPTANCE CLAIMS AND ORACLES. (1) Numbers and times are correct given the supplied inputs — oracle: the supplied documents, recomputed independently. (2) Nothing in the schedule comes from outside those inputs, and every real gap/conflict is flagged rather than resolved — oracle: the same documents read parameter-by-parameter, but the observation is traceability/enumeration, not recomputation. (3) Conduct constraints — oracle: the artifact's own assertions (fully observable) plus reachable messaging surfaces' attributable sent records.

WHY THREE VALIDATORS, NOT ONE. Starting from one cohesive validator, the split from recomputation to traceability is earned by a concrete defect each would miss alone. Planted defect A: weight 18.4 kg x 7.5 mg/kg rendered as 128 mg instead of 138 mg. dose-schedule-recomputation catches it — it computes 138 and compares, a hard numeric mismatch. input-traceability would not necessarily catch it: 128 is a plausible product and that validator's job is locating parameters, not multiplying every row. Planted defect B: the prescription says q6h while the dosing table caps daily total below 4 x that dose, and the artifact silently truncates the last dose to fit without flagging the conflict. input-traceability catches it — it enumerates both sources, finds them in disagreement on a schedule-determining parameter, and finds no flag. dose-schedule-recomputation can approve it, because a recomputation that also honours the cap reproduces the same truncated numbers; the two agents can agree on a wrong resolution. Merging them loses one of these checks, so the split is real. They share a stage and run in parallel because their cost is comparable.

WHY THE CONDUCT GATE IS SEPARATE AND IN STAGE 1. Its failure mode (the artifact asserts a clinician reviewed/approved this schedule, or asserts it messaged the patient or administered a dose, or an attributable outbound message to the patient exists) is observed against a different oracle — artifact assertions and messaging-tool records — not the clinical documents. It is a short read plus a bounded outbox check versus two full independent recomputations of a 24h schedule against multi-source documents, and a violation makes the arithmetic moot: a schedule that falsely claims clinician sign-off is unusable no matter how correct its numbers. That is a genuine cost saving, not a mechanical/evaluative split. Planted defect: the line "reviewed and approved by the prescribing physician" or "I have texted the patient the schedule" — the gate reads it verbatim and rejects.

FALSE-REJECT AUDIT. A different but compliant artifact passes all three. Recomputation is bound to presentation-independence: any layout, clock format, ordering, filename or medium approves as long as the values match, and rounding is judged only against a rounding rule stated in the inputs, so no invented tolerance and no invented format requirement. Traceability accepts any wording, position, count or severity scheme for flags and explicitly accepts values derived through input-authorized transformations (mg/kg x kg, unit conversions), so a correctly derived number is not called untraceable. Both are barred from importing outside clinical knowledge — a dose that looks unusual against general practice but follows the supplied table must be approved, which also stops the validators from doing the clinical resolution the task forbids. The conduct gate explicitly must not reject the requested schedule for reading like dose instructions (that is the deliverable), must not reject restating that the supplied prescription was clinician-authored, and must not reject a draft that was never claimed sent. None of the three asks what changed, who acted historically, what existed before, or requires a self-authored evidence log from the worker — validators obtain their own evidence from the supplied inputs. No preservation claim exists in this task, so no baseline is needed.

EVIDENCE GAPS PRESERVED. "Did not message the patient" is a negative side-effect claim; current state cannot attribute an actor. The gate rejects only on an attributable record or the artifact's own claim of having done it, and where messaging surfaces are unreachable it must return EVIDENCE GAP rather than either approving or accusing. Likewise, if the supplied source material is not reachable, both stage-2 validators return EVIDENCE GAP rather than falling back to plausibility review — recomputation without the source table is not verification.

IMPLEMENTATION PROMPT AUDIT. It carries only task-derived requirements: use only the supplied inputs, express times in the supplied timezone, flag rather than resolve, deliver the determinable portion, honour the four negative constraints, and do not refuse work the inputs fully determine. No filename, section layout, table format, citation scheme, evidence log, flag taxonomy or tooling is mandated, and no verifier probe was promoted into an executor requirement.

agents.purpose: Calculate the next 24 hours of dose times and amounts from the supplied prescription, dosing table, weight and timezone, flagging conflicts and missing inputs.
agents.systemPrompt:
You calculate a dosing schedule from supplied material. You run non-interactively: there is no user to ask, so never ask a question and never wait for confirmation. Make decisions and proceed.

INPUTS. Locate the material supplied with this task: the prescription, the dosing table, the patient weight, and the timezone. Discover where that material actually is (attached text, files, or whatever was provided with the task) rather than assuming a path or filename. These supplied items are your ONLY authority. Do not consult external sources, reference ranges, clinical guidelines, formularies, or your own clinical knowledge, and do not substitute a default, a standard practice value, or a 'typical' value for anything the supplied material does not state.

WHAT TO PRODUCE. The dose times and amounts for the next 24 hours, expressed unambiguously in the supplied timezone. Derive the anchor for 'next 24 hours' from the supplied material (for example a start time, a last-dose time, or the request time in the supplied timezone). If the supplied material does not determine the anchor, flag that as a missing input rather than choosing one. If a daylight-saving transition falls in the window, handle it according to the supplied timezone.

FLAG, DO NOT RESOLVE. Wherever the supplied material is missing a value the schedule depends on, or two supplied sources disagree, or a value is ambiguous, state that plainly as a conflict or missing input and do not settle it. Do not resolve it clinically, do not pick the safer option, do not average, and do not fill the gap from outside knowledge. Where a gap blocks only part of the schedule, still deliver the part the supplied inputs fully determine and flag the rest. Conversely, do not flag something the supplied inputs do actually determine, and do not refuse to perform a calculation the supplied inputs fully support: producing the determinable schedule is required.

HARD CONSTRAINTS. Do not administer anything. Do not prescribe, change, or add therapy. Do not message, contact, or notify the patient or anyone else, and do not send or publish anything through any external system. Do not state or imply that a clinician has reviewed, approved, or signed off on your calculation; you may accurately restate facts about the supplied prescription itself, but not attribute approval to your output.

FORMAT. Choose your own presentation. No particular filename, layout, table structure, or section scheme is required. Complete work only: no placeholders, TODOs, or deferrals in the delivered schedule.
